Truncations.description:
DIV{HEADER1{Truncations,  -- truncations of graded ring, ideals and modules}, DIV{HEADER2{Description}, DIV{PARA{TEX{This package provides methods for truncation of a graded ring, or a graded module or ideal over a graded ring (see }, TO{Macaulay2Doc :: truncate(List,Module)}, TEX{). Truncation is functorial: it can be applied to maps of modules as well, and the truncation of a composition of maps is the composition of the truncations (see }, TO{Macaulay2Doc :: truncate(List,Matrix)}, TEX{).}}, PARA{TEX{Let $S$ be a $\ZZ^r$-graded ring whose variables have non-negative degrees and $M$ be a graded $S$-module. Then for a finite subset of degrees $L\subset\ZZ^r$ the method , TT{truncate(L, M)},  computes $$M_{\ge L} = \bigoplus_{m\in L+\NN^r} M_m,$$ where the sum is taken over all degrees $m \in \ZZ^r$ which are component-wise greater than or equal to some degree $d\in L$. In this case the truncation is a submodule of $M$.}}}, TABLE{class => examples, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{i1 : R = ZZ/101[a..d, Degrees => {1,2,3,4}];, class => language-macaulay2}}}}, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{i2 : truncate(4, ideal"a3,b3")

             4   3    3    3   3
o2 = ideal (a , a b, a c, b , a d)

o2 : Ideal of R, class => language-macaulay2}}}}}, DIV{PARA{TEX{More generally, let $S$ be the total coordinate ring of a simplicial toric variety $X$ with Picard group $\operatorname{Pic} X$. Then for a finite subset $L\subset\operatorname{Pic} X$, the truncation $F_{\ge L}$ of a free module $F$ may be defined as the submodule generated by $$F_{\ge L} = \bigoplus_{m\in L+\operatorname{Nef} X} F_m,$$ where $\operatorname{Nef} X$ is the semigroup of nef line bundles in $\operatorname{Pic} X$ (c.f. Definition 5.1 in [MS04]). Then for a graded $S$-module $M$ with }, TO{Macaulay2Doc :: presentation}, TEX{ $0 \gets M \gets G \gets H,$ where $G$ and $H$ are free modules, the truncation $M_{\ge L}$ is the $S$-module with presentation $$0 \gets M_{\ge L} \gets G_{\ge L} \gets H_{\ge L}.$$ Note that $M_{\ge L}$ is not a submodule of $M$ in general, but exact sequences are preserved and since $M/M_{\ge L}$ is annihilated by a power of the irrelevant ideal of $S$, a module and its truncation define the same sheaf.}}}, TABLE{class => examples, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{i3 : needsPackage "NormalToricVarieties";, class => language-macaulay2}}}}, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{i4 : dP6 = smoothFanoToricVariety(2, 4);, class => language-macaulay2}}}}, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{i5 : S = ring dP6;, class => language-macaulay2}}}}, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{i6 : M = S^{-{0,0,1,0}};, class => language-macaulay2}}}}, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{i7 : N = truncate({0,0,0,0}, M)

o7 = image {0, 0, 1, 0} | x_4 x_2 |

                             1
o7 : S-module, submodule of S, class => language-macaulay2}}}}, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{i8 : N == coker truncate({0,0,0,0}, presentation M)

o8 = true, class => language-macaulay2}}}}}, DIV{PARA{TEX{For the most general case, if $S$ is a $\ZZ^r$-graded ring where the degree components of variables may be negative, the result is the same as the above but we fix the nef cone to be the positive orthant $\NN^r$.}}}, TABLE{class => examples, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{i9 : R = ZZ/101[a..d, Degrees => {2:{1,0},{0,1},{-3,1}}];, class => language-macaulay2}}}}, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{i10 : M = R^1/ideal d

o10 = cokernel | d |

                             1
o10 : R-module, quotient of R, class => language-macaulay2}}}}, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{i11 : N = truncate({0,0}, M)

o11 = cokernel | b3d ab2d a2bd a3d |

                             1
o11 : R-module, quotient of R, class => language-macaulay2}}}}, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{i12 : isSubset(M, N)

o12 = false, class => language-macaulay2}}}}}, DIV{PARA{TEX{The polyhedral algorithms implemented in this package correctly handle many cases. The behavior of }, TO{Macaulay2Doc :: truncate}, TEX{ changed as of Macaulay2 version 1.13 to support }, TO{Macaulay2Doc :: exterior algebras}, TEX{, and again in Macaulay2 version 1.19 to support Cox rings of simplicial }, TO2{NormalToricVarieties :: NormalToricVarieties, normal toric varieties}, TEX{.}}}}, DIV{HEADER2{Contributors}, DIV{PARA{TEX{Lauren Cranton Heller contributed to the code and documentation for this package.}}}}, DIV{HEADER2{References}, DIV{UL{LI{[MS04]: Maclagan and Smith, Multigraded Castelnuovo-Mumford Regularity (see , HREF{https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0305214, arXiv:math/0305214}, ).}}}}, DIV{HEADER2{See also}, UL{LI{TOH{Macaulay2Doc :: basis}}}}, MENU{UL{LI{TOH{Macaulay2Doc :: truncate(List,Module)}}, LI{TOH{Macaulay2Doc :: truncate(List,Matrix)}}}}, DIV{DIV{DIV{HEADER2{Authors}, UL{LI{HREF{https://www.msri.org/~de, David Eisenbud}, SPAN{ <, HREF{mailto:de@msri.org, de@msri.org}, >}}, LI{HREF{https://www.math.cornell.edu/~mike, Mike Stillman}, SPAN{ <, HREF{mailto:mike@math.cornell.edu, mike@math.cornell.edu}, >}}, LI{HREF{https://math.umn.edu/~mahrud, Mahrud Sayrafi}, SPAN{ <, HREF{mailto:mahrud@umn.edu, mahrud@umn.edu}, >}}}}, DIV{HEADER2{Version}, PARA{This documentation describes version , BOLD{1.0},  of , Truncations, , released , BOLD{22 May 2021}, .}}, DIV{HEADER2{Citation}, PARA{If you have used , this package,  in your research, please cite it as follows:}, TABLE{class => examples, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{class => language-bib, @misc{TruncationsSource,
  title = {{Truncations: truncation of a module. Version~1.0}},
  author = {David Eisenbud and Mike Stillman and Mahrud Sayrafi},
  howpublished = {A \emph{Macaulay2} package available at
    \url{https://github.com/Macaulay2/M2/tree/stable/M2/Macaulay2/packages}}
}
}}}}}}, DIV{HEADER2{Exports}, DIV{class => exports, UL{LI{Functions and commands}, LI{Methods, UL{LI{TOH{Truncations :: truncate(List,Matrix)}}, LI{SPAN{KBD{truncate(ZZ,Matrix)},  -- see , TOH{Truncations :: truncate(List,Matrix)}}}, LI{SPAN{KBD{truncate(List,Ideal)},  -- see , TOH{Truncations :: truncate(List,Module)}}}, LI{TOH{Truncations :: truncate(List,Module)}}, LI{SPAN{KBD{truncate(List,Ring)},  -- see , TOH{Truncations :: truncate(List,Module)}}}, LI{SPAN{KBD{truncate(ZZ,Ideal)},  -- see , TOH{Truncations :: truncate(List,Module)}}}, LI{SPAN{KBD{truncate(ZZ,Module)},  -- see , TOH{Truncations :: truncate(List,Module)}}}, LI{SPAN{KBD{truncate(ZZ,Ring)},  -- see , TOH{Truncations :: truncate(List,Module)}}}}}}}}}, DIV{class => waystouse, HEADER2{For the programmer}, PARA{The object , TO{Truncations :: Truncations},  is , SPAN{a , TO2{Macaulay2Doc :: Package, package}}, , defined in , TT{Truncations.m2}, , with auxiliary files in , TT{Truncations/}, .}}, HR{}, DIV{class => waystouse, PARA{The source of this document is in , TT{Truncations/docs.m2:229:0}, .}}}}

Up.description:
DIV{HEADER1{Up,  -- monomial ordering}, DIV{HEADER2{Description}, TT{MonomialOrder},  -- an optional argument used with polynomial rings and monoids to indicate a monomial ordering other than the default (graded reverse lexicographic)., PARA{}, In Macaulay2, each polynomial ring (and also each monoid) is equipped with a monomial order, which is used for display of polynomials (terms are listed in descending monomial order), and also for Gröbner basis computations., PARA{}, In the most general setting, a monomial ordering is given by a list of , EM{ordering tests}, , of various types listed and described below, each of which provides a partial ordering on the monomials.  The ordering tests are applied sequentially, starting with the first one, until one monomial is judged greater than the other. At the end, if necessary, the graded reverse lexicographic order is used to compare the monomials. For examples, see below, or see , TO{Macaulay2Doc :: monomial orderings}, ., PARA{}, Permissible elements:, UL{LI{TO{Macaulay2Doc :: GRevLex},  => n -- A graded reverse lexicographic block of variables}, LI{TO{Macaulay2Doc :: Lex},  => n}, LI{TO{Macaulay2Doc :: Weights},  => {...}}, LI{TO{Macaulay2Doc :: Position},  => Up  or  Position => Down}, LI{TO{Macaulay2Doc :: RevLex},  => n}, LI{TO{Macaulay2Doc :: GroupLex},  => n}, LI{TO{Macaulay2Doc :: GroupRevLex},  => n}, LI{TO{Macaulay2Doc :: MonomialSize},  => n, n being 8,16,32, or 64.  Set the packing size for exponents for further variables}}, PARA{}, Some examples of monomial orders.  Note that if only one item is in the list, we can dispense with the list., UL{LI{TT{MonomialOrder => {GRevLex=>2, GRevLex=>3}},  -- a product order}, LI{TT{MonomialOrder => {2, 3}},  -- same}, LI{TT{MonomialOrder => {Weights=>{1,13,6,2}}},  -- a weight order}, LI{TT{MonomialOrder => Weights=>{1,13,6,2}},  -- same}}, If any monomials will be less than 1 in the ordering, then the option , TT{Global => false},  should be used., TABLE{class => examples, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{i1 : QQ[x,y, Weights => {-1,1}, Global => false]

o1 = QQ[x..y]

o1 : PolynomialRing, class => language-macaulay2}}}}, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{i2 : x<1

o2 = true, class => language-macaulay2}}}}, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{i3 : y<1

o3 = false, class => language-macaulay2}}}}}}, DIV{HEADER2{See also}, UL{LI{TOH{Macaulay2Doc :: monomial orderings}}, LI{TOH{QthPower :: weightGrevlex}}, LI{TOH{QthPower :: grevlexWeight}}}}, DIV{DIV{class => waystouse, HEADER2{For the programmer}, PARA{The object , TO{Macaulay2Doc :: Up},  is , SPAN{a , TO2{Macaulay2Doc :: Symbol, symbol}}, .}}, HR{}, DIV{class => waystouse, PARA{The source of this document is in , TT{Macaulay2Doc/ov_monomial_orderings.m2:704:0}, .}}}}

DIV{HEADER1{versalEmbedding,  -- Compute a versal embedding}, UL{LI{DL{class => element, DT{Usage: }, DD{CODE{u = versalEmbedding M, class => language-macaulay2}}}}, LI{Inputs:, UL{LI{SPAN{TT{M}, , , SPAN{a , TO2{Macaulay2Doc :: Module, module}}, , , TEX{or }, SPAN{an , TO2{Macaulay2Doc :: Ideal, ideal}}}}}}, LI{Outputs:, UL{LI{SPAN{TT{u}, , , SPAN{a , TO2{Macaulay2Doc :: Matrix, matrix}}, , , TEX{a matrix that induces a versal embedding of the R-module M into a free R-module.}}}}}}, DIV{HEADER2{Description}, DIV{PARA{TEX{For any module M over a Noetherian ring R there is a map $u: M \to H$ that is versal for maps from M to free modules; that is, such that any map from M to a free module factors through u. Such a map may be constructed by choosing a set of s generators for Hom(M,R), and using them as the components of a map $u: M \to H := R^s$.}}, PARA{TEX{(NOTE: In the paper of  Eisenbud, Huneke and Ulrich cited below, the versal map is described with the term ``universal'', which is misleading, since the induced map from H is generally not unique.)}}, PARA{TEX{Suppose that $M$ has a free presentation $F \to G$, and let $u1$ be the map $u1: G\to H$ induced by composing $u$ with the surjection $p: G \to M$.  By definition, the Rees algebra of $M$ is the image of the induced map $Sym(u1): Sym(G)\to Sym(H)$, and thus can be computed with symmetricKernel(u1).  The map u is computed from the dual of the first syzygy map of the dual of the presentation of $M$.}}, PARA{TEX{We first give a simple example looking at the syzygy matrix of the cube of the maximal ideal of a polynomial ring.}}}, TABLE{class => examples, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{i1 : S = ZZ/101[x,y,z];, class => language-macaulay2}}}}, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{i2 : FF=res ((ideal vars S)^3);, class => language-macaulay2}}}}, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{i3 : M=coker (FF.dd_2)

              {3} | 0  0  0  0  0  x  y  -y 0  0  -z 0  0  0  0  |
              {3} | 0  0  0  0  0  0  0  x  y  0  0  0  -z 0  0  |
              {3} | 0  0  0  0  0  0  0  0  0  x  y  -y 0  -z 0  |

Weights.description:
DIV{HEADER1{Weights,  -- assigning weights to the variables}, DIV{HEADER2{Description}, Given a list L of n integers, the weight order on a polynomial ring in n variables is defined by: x^A > x^B if A_1 L_1 + ... + A_n L_n > B_1 L_1 + ... + B_n L_n., PARA{}, The leading component of a polynomial under a weight order need not be a monomial.  When two monomials have the same weight, by default they are further distinguished with the GRevLex order., TABLE{class => examples, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{i1 : R = QQ[a..d,MonomialOrder=>{Weights => {-1,2,3,4}},Global=>false];, class => language-macaulay2}}}}, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{i2 : f = a^2 + b+ c^2 + b*d

      2              2
o2 = c  + b*d + b + a

o2 : R, class => language-macaulay2}}}}, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{i3 : leadTerm f

      2
o3 = c

o3 : R, class => language-macaulay2}}}}}, However, we can retrieve the entire leading component with the command , TT{leadTerm(1,f)}, . The plain , TT{leadTerm f},  is in this case the same as , TT{leadTerm(2,f)}, : they both use the full specification of the monomial ordering, first by weight and then by the , TT{GRevLex},  order.  In contrast, , TT{leadTerm(1,f)}, only distinguishes monomials by the first, i.e., weight, specification., TABLE{class => examples, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{i4 : leadTerm(1,ideal(f))

            2
o4 = ideal(c  + b*d)

o4 : Ideal of R, class => language-macaulay2}}}}}, The weight order may be combined with further ordering elements to break ties. In the following example, we use a second weight vector to break ties under first weight vector., TABLE{class => examples, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{i5 : R = QQ[a..d,MonomialOrder=>{Weights => {1,2,3,4}, Weights => {2,4,2,1}}];, class => language-macaulay2}}}}, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{i6 : f = a^6 + b^3+ c^2

      6    3    2
o6 = a  + b  + c

o6 : R, class => language-macaulay2}}}}, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{i7 : leadTerm(f)

      6
o7 = a

o7 : R, class => language-macaulay2}}}}, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{i8 : leadTerm(1, ideal(f))

            6    3    2
o8 = ideal(a  + b  + c )

o8 : Ideal of R, class => language-macaulay2}}}}, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{i9 : leadTerm(2, ideal(f))

            6    3
o9 = ideal(a  + b )

o9 : Ideal of R, class => language-macaulay2}}}}, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{i10 : leadTerm(3, ideal(f))

             6
o10 = ideal a

o10 : Ideal of R, class => language-macaulay2}}}}}, TT{leadTerm(3, ideal(f))},  uses both the specified weights and the , TT{GRevLex},  order to calculate the leading component., PARA{}, When the number of weights is smaller than the number of variables, the remaining variables are given weight 0. In the following example, , TT{c},  and , TT{d},  have weight 0., TABLE{class => examples, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{i11 : R = QQ[a..d,MonomialOrder=>{Weights => {1,2}, Lex}];, class => language-macaulay2}}}}, TR{TD{PRE{CODE{i12 : f = a^2 + b+ c^2 + b*d

       2              2
o12 = a  + b*d + b + c

o12 : R, class => language-macaulay2}}}}}}, DIV{HEADER2{See also}, UL{LI{TOH{Macaulay2Doc :: leadTerm}}}}, DIV{DIV{HEADER2{Functions with optional argument named , TT{Weights}, :}, UL{LI{SPAN{KBD{betti(...,Weights=>...)},  -- see , TOH{Macaulay2Doc :: betti(BettiTally)}}}, LI{SPAN{KBD{minimalBetti(...,Weights=>...)},  -- see , TOH{Macaulay2Doc :: minimalBetti}}}, LI{TOH{Macaulay2Doc :: monoid(...,Weights=>...)}}, LI{SPAN{KBD{newRing(...,Weights=>...)},  -- see , TOH{Macaulay2Doc :: newRing}}}, LI{SPAN{KBD{regularity(...,Weights=>...)},  -- see , TOH{Macaulay2Doc :: regularity}}}, LI{SPAN{KBD{symmetricAlgebra(...,Weights=>...)},  -- see , TOH{Macaulay2Doc :: symmetricAlgebra}}}, LI{SPAN{KBD{tensor(Monoid,Monoid,Weights=>...)},  -- see , TOH{Macaulay2Doc :: tensor(Monoid,Monoid)}}}, LI{SPAN{KBD{tensor(Ring,Ring,Weights=>...)},  -- see , TOH{Macaulay2Doc :: tensor(Monoid,Monoid)}}}}}, DIV{class => waystouse, HEADER2{For the programmer}, PARA{The object , TO{Macaulay2Doc :: Weights},  is , SPAN{a , TO2{Macaulay2Doc :: Symbol, symbol}}, .}}, HR{}, DIV{class => waystouse, PARA{The source of this document is in , TT{Macaulay2Doc/ov_monomial_orderings.m2:515:0}, .}}}}
